title: KILN: the Firing Dial
concept: Two potters share one 4x4 kiln. A single printed dial holds sixteen firing bands in a secret order; each turn you turn it and obey the band the fire demands. Every disc you glaze changes which shapes you can reach before the kiln is full. But only you know the two glaze rituals you are trying to complete, and only you know how much each is worth — so the same open board hides two different games being played at once.

design_contract.core_experience: A tense two-player territorial packing duel in which public dial constraints collide with private hidden objectives, so both players optimise different boards at once.
design_contract.core_mechanism: A shared linear dial of sixteen firing bands is shuffled once and turned one band per turn. Each band forces the active player's placement: OPEN anywhere, SHY away from rival discs, REGION beside your own disc, FAR away from your own disc. Each player additionally holds two hidden objective tiles worth secret bonus points for completing specific shapes on the finished tray.
must_preserve: The firing dial is a single rotating printed wheel, public to both players, whose band order is fixed at setup.
Each player's two objective tiles are visible only to them until scoring, creating simultaneous asymmetric play on one shared board.
The tray fills after exactly 16 placements with 8 discs per player, so material parity is structural, never adjudicated.
Regions of orthogonally connected own-colour discs score size squared; satisfied hidden objective tiles add secret bonuses.
anti_goals: No cards, dice, app or moderator.
No hidden dial information: both players must always see the dial position and the revealed band.
No rule that lets a player move or remove a disc once glazed.
kill_criteria: A competent first seat exceeds a 10 percentage-point advantage after simulation.
The game draws (ties) more than 10 percent of competent self-play games.
Players face fewer than 3 meaningful placement choices on average (median branching below 3).
A full set cannot be printed on a 160 x 160 mm bed without supports or split parts.

novelty: KILN does not claim the broad idea of hidden objectives or territorial area scoring — both are ancient. Its narrower, printable combination is the shared firing dial as the ONLY public information (a single shuffled wheel, turned one band per turn, forcing either OPEN/SHY/REGION/FAR placements) combined with fully concealed asymmetric victory tiles on a symmetric 4x4 shared tray, where material parity is structural (8 discs each) rather than adjudicated. Searches on 2026-08-23 found no tabletop product titled KILN or KILN: the Firing Dial; this is a product-search result, not trademark or freedom-to-operate clearance. Full sources and limits travel with the downloadable page at docs/prior-art.md.

art_direction.form_language: Everything is baked-clay geometry: the shared tray is a thick slab with sixteen recessed glaze wells, its corners radiused like a kiln shelf. The dial is a low faceted wheel with a knurled rim and one raised pointer, printed to rotate on a central boss. The discs are fat shallow bungs with a knurled top lip so they can be picked up even when the tray is crowded.
art_direction.silhouette: A slab of cracked sienna loam dotted with two colours of glazed bungs, one low faceted dial at its edge where the fire is read, and two small screens sheltering each player's ritual tiles.
art_direction.part_vocabulary: FOUR families, each separable by shape alone at arm's length. (1) kiln_tray — the only flat, wide, cracked thing, a 144 x 144 x 26 mm slab of sixteen recessed wells. (2) kiln_dial — the only rotating thing, a faceted wheel with a pointer on a central boss; one shared dial per game. (3) glaze_disc — the only round bung; 16 discs, 8 per colour, fat with a knurled lip. (4) ritual_screen — two small freestanding screens with a notch, sheltering the objective tiles.
art_direction.surface_treatment: The tray top is crosshatched with 1.0 mm fine crazing so it reads as fired clay, never a plain plate. Each glaze well has a chamfered rim. The dial pointer and band pips are at least 0.8 mm proud. Disc knurl is 0.9 mm. No motif is under 0.8 mm.
art_direction.hero_shot: The full tray moments before the final glaze: sixteen wells, two colours nearly settled into interlocking regions, the faceted dial mid-turn with a pointer resting on a band, and just visible at the table's edge the two screens behind which each potter hides a different ambition.

components.name: kiln_tray
components.desc: A 144 x 144 x 26 mm slab of fired loam with sixteen recessed glaze wells in a 4x4 grid, each well chamfered and arranged so the tray is separable by shape alone. One shared tray per game; prints on a single 160 x 160 mm bed with no supports.

components.name: kiln_dial
components.desc: A faceted low wheel, about 62 mm across, with a knurled rim, one raised pointer, and a set of sixteen band pips around its edge. It rotates on a fixed central boss at the tray's corner. The band order is set by the shuffle at setup and is public.

components.name: glaze_disc
components.desc: A fat round bung about 18 mm across with a knurled top lip, flat-bottomed so it seats cleanly in a glaze well. Eight per player in their own colour. Kerbing on the top lip lets it be lifted even from a full tray.

components.name: ritual_screen
components.desc: A small freestanding L-shaped screen with a notch; one per player, sheltering the two objective tiles so only the owner sees them. The screen reads as a kiln hood.

objective_tiles: CORNERS: own all four corner wells.
ROW3: own three consecutive wells in any row.
COL3: own three consecutive wells in any column.
BLOCK: own a full 2x2 block of wells.
CENTER: own the four centre wells.
EDGE3: own at least three wells on the outer rim.

setup.text: Place the shared kiln_tray between the players and the kiln_dial at its corner. Shuffle the sixteen firing bands privately behind a screen and load them onto the dial in that random order; this order is now public.
Each player takes eight glaze_discs of their colour and one ritual_screen, and draws two distinct objective tiles from the six, hiding them behind their screen.
Choose the first player at random. The first player turns the dial to reveal the first band, then places one of their discs.

turn.text: Play continues with players alternating turns. On your turn, turn the dial forward one band and read it aloud; it is public. Then place exactly one of your discs in an empty well under that band's constraint.

Bands: OPEN = any empty well; SHY = a well not orthogonally adjacent to a rival disc; REGION = a well orthogonally adjacent to one of your own discs; FAR = a well not orthogonally adjacent to one of your own discs.
If a band has no legal well for you, place in any empty well instead. A disc, once placed, never moves.

end.text: After sixteen placements the tray is full (eight discs each). Each player in turn reveals their two objective tiles and checks whether each is satisfied on the finished tray.
Score each player's orthogonally connected regions of their own colour: each region of size n is worth n x n. Then add each satisfied objective's bonus. Highest total wins.

win.text: Add your region size-squared scores to your satisfied objective bonuses. Highest total wins. On a tie, the player with the higher region-only score (objectives removed) wins; if still tied, the win is shared.
